claim: Buildroot's download page lists 2025.02.x as the long-term-support series (EOL March 2028; latest 2025.02.19 released 2026-10-22), the stable series as 2026.08.1 (EOL December 2026) and 2026.05.x as EOL September 2026; 2026.02 is not an LTS series.

Buildroot's pc_x86_64_efi_defconfig pins Linux 6.1.24 at tag 2025.02.19 and Linux 6.12.47 at tag 2026.02.3: board demo defconfigs carry stale kernel pins, so a product must set and track its own kernel version.
Buildroot 2025.02.19's linux/linux.hash carries hashes up to Linux 6.12.112 for the 6.12 series; using a newer point release (6.12.117) needs the hash check relaxed or a local hash added.
kernel.org lists 6.12.117 (released 2026-11-10) as the current 6.12 longterm point release; Debian 13.7 ships kernel 6.12.116 (package 6.12.116-1).
Debian 13 (trixie) ships mkosi 25.3-7; forky/sid have 27.1-1.
k3s v1.37.2+k3s1 (published 2026-11-03) is the k3s stable channel release on 2026-11-11.
syft v1.57.1 and grype v0.121.3 were both published 2026-11-09; the grype vulnerability DB used for every scan in this spike is schema v6.1.10, built 2026-11-11T06:21:32Z.

[Lab, x86_64, Lima VM 12 vCPU on Apple M5 Max shared with three other lab VMs; one run each] Build times: Debian 13 via mkosi 25.3: 180 s clean with downloads, 203 s clean with package cache, 49 s incremental; Buildroot 2025.02.19: 1716 s clean with downloads, 779 s clean with downloads cached, 29 s after one package change, 102 s for a kernel point-release bump.

[Lab] Installed root filesystem without k3s: Debian 293.6 MB vs Buildroot 82.4 MB (3.6x); with the ESP (Debian's 155.6 MB UKI with initrd vs Buildroot's 9.8 MB) 449.1 MB vs 92.2 MB (4.9x); zstd-19 tarball of the root without k3s 154.5 MB vs 27.1 MB (5.7x); with the 81.7 MB k3s binary, root 375.3 MB vs 164.1 MB (2.3x).

[Lab] SBOM: syft finds 139 Debian binary packages (85 source packages) plus 4230 kernel modules in the Debian image, but only 2 binaries, the kernel and 59 modules in the Buildroot image; Buildroot's own CycloneDX (utils/generate-cyclonedx) lists 27 target packages plus 60 build-host tools (scope excluded). A filesystem scanner is close to blind on a Buildroot image; the build system's SBOM is the only complete one.

[Lab, grype DB 2026-11-11] Without k3s, Debian has 589 unique CVE IDs (186 Critical+High); Buildroot's target SBOM has 549 (195 C+H), or 498 (175 C+H) after removing matches that Buildroot's own SBOM marks resolved (patched/ignored). That is 7-15% fewer IDs and -5% to +6% C+H: far from the pre-registered 50% 'materially fewer' threshold.

[Lab] The kernel is 73-80% of all CVE IDs in both legs and depends on the kernel version, not the build method: Debian's 6.12.116 and Buildroot's 6.12.117 both match 428 kernel CVE IDs (149 C+H); Buildroot's 6.12.112 matches 440.

[Lab] Userspace CVEs: Debian 161 unique IDs, every one triaged by Debian's tracker as not-fixed (74) or wont-fix (87), so 0 have an available fix; Buildroot 2025.02.19 has 58 (minus resolved) to 109, of which 32-53 have an upstream fix not yet in the LTS (e.g. OpenSSH 9.9p2, glibc 2.41, util-linux 2.40.4, systemd 256.17). Buildroot's list is shorter but is real patch backlog that OneMind would own; some CPE matches are false positives (OpenSSH 'fixed in 9.9p2' reported against 9.9p2).

[Lab] The k3s v1.37.2+k3s1 binary adds 18 Go modules and 1 vulnerability ID (github.com/klauspost/compress) to a syft/grype scan of the image, the same in both legs; the payload k3s unpacks at first start (containerd, runc, CNI plugins, a busybox userland) is not visible to that scan (see C-LAB-minimal-image-dc20-020).

[Lab] An incremental Buildroot kernel bump (6.12.112 to 6.12.117) left the old kernel's /lib/modules/6.12.112 (7.7 MB) in the image; Buildroot incremental builds do not remove stale target files, so release images need clean builds.

[Lab] A mkosi 25.3 Debian disk image with no Locale/Timezone/root settings runs systemd-firstboot at first boot and waits for console input, so an unattended appliance image must set them (or disable firstboot).

[Lab] On the Debian 13 image (kernel 6.12.116 with AppArmor enabled) `k3s check-config` (v1.37.2+k3s1) returns STATUS fail with 'apparmor: enabled, but apparmor_parser missing'; adding the apparmor package (+2.8 MB, 0 new CVE IDs) makes it pass. On the Buildroot image it passes. Both nodes reached Ready 40 s after k3s started (QEMU TCG).
[Lab] Buildroot 2025.02.19 defaults to an empty root password (BR2_TARGET_GENERIC_ROOT_PASSWD="") and its kernel banner records the build user@host; the mkosi Debian image ships root locked ('*').

[Lab, single sample, QEMU TCG x86_64 on arm64, 4 GiB guest] Buildroot reached multi-user at uptime 8.6 s vs Debian 43.1 s (Debian's UKI carries a 130.6 MB generic initrd); used RAM after k3s Ready was 381 MB vs 653 MB.

[Lab] The k3s v1.37.2+k3s1 data payload unpacked at first start is 283.6 MB and syft finds 515 components in it (514 Go modules); grype reports 22 vulnerability IDs (8 High), 13 with a fix available, none of which a pre-boot image scan shows.

[Lab] DC-20 pre-registered flip test: Buildroot's CVE reduction vs Debian (without k3s) is 6.8-17.5% in unique IDs and -8.6% to +4.8% in Critical+High, against a pre-registered 50% threshold, so the 'materially fewer CVEs' clause of the W3 steelman's flip condition is not met; the '< 1 h incremental build' clause is met (29 s package, 102 s kernel bump); the CUDA clause was not tested.
